# Reference design for Graph Connectivity and Network Reliability Analyzer

## Architecture
Use adjacency lists and DFS discovery/low-link times to identify bridges and articulation points. Treat a disconnected graph by launching DFS from every unseen vertex.

## Algorithm/design sketch
The protected bridge/articulation exercise solution provides an undirected simple-graph baseline. For multigraphs, use edge IDs so parallel edges are not confused with the parent edge.

## Complexity targets
Connected components O(V+E); bridges/articulation points O(V+E); Kruskal MST O(E log E).

## Reference code excerpt
```python
def bridges_and_articulation_points(graph):
    """Undirected simple graph represented as {vertex: [neighbors]}.
    For multigraphs, track edge IDs so parallel edges are handled correctly.
    """
    timer=0; tin={}; low={}; bridges=[]; articulation=set()
    def dfs(v,parent,root=False):
        nonlocal timer
        tin[v]=low[v]=timer; timer+=1; children=0
        for u in graph[v]:
            if u==parent: continue
            if u in tin: low[v]=min(low[v],tin[u])
            else:
                dfs(u,v); low[v]=min(low[v],low[u]); children+=1
                if low[u]>tin[v]: bridges.append((v,u))
                if parent is not None and low[u]>=tin[v]: articulation.add(v)
        if root and children>1: articulation.add(v)
    for v in graph:
        if v not in tin: dfs(v,None,True)
    return bridges, articulation

b,a=bridges_and_articulation_points({0:[1],1:[0,2],2:[1]})
assert len(b)==2 and a=={1}
```
